title: Fluffy Buttermilk Pancakes
description: Tall, tender weekend pancakes with a slight tang from buttermilk. The batter comes together in minutes and the pancakes freeze well for weekday breakfasts.
steps: Whisk the flour, sugar, baking powder, salt, and baking soda in a large bowl.
In a separate bowl, whisk the buttermilk, eggs, melted butter, and vanilla.
Pour the wet ingredients into the dry and stir until just combined. Lumps are good; overmixing is not.
Heat a lightly buttered pan over medium heat. Pour 80 ml rounds of batter.
Cook until bubbles pop on the surface, 2-3 minutes, then flip and cook until golden, another 1-2 minutes.
Keep warm in a low oven while you cook the rest. Serve with maple syrup.

title: Shakshuka
description: Eggs poached in a smoky spiced tomato sauce, a one-pan breakfast or easy dinner. Good bread for scooping is non-negotiable.
steps: Warm the oil in a skillet over medium heat and soften the onion and pepper, 8-10 minutes.
Add the garlic and spices and cook until fragrant, about a minute.
Pour in the tomatoes, season with salt and pepper, and simmer until thickened, 10 minutes.
Make four wells in the sauce and crack an egg into each.
Cover and cook until the whites are set but the yolks are still soft, 5-7 minutes.
Scatter over the parsley and serve straight from the pan with bread.

title: Overnight Oats
description: Five minutes of work tonight, breakfast waiting tomorrow. The ratio is the whole recipe; everything else is riffing.
steps: Stir the oats, milk, yogurt, and honey together in a jar.
Cover and refrigerate overnight (or at least 4 hours).
Top with the almonds and berries and eat cold.

title: Spaghetti Aglio e Olio
description: The original pantry pasta: garlic, oil, chili, and parsley. It succeeds or fails on patience, so take the garlic slowly.
steps: Boil the spaghetti in well-salted water until al dente. Reserve 250 ml of pasta water.
Meanwhile, warm the oil with the garlic over low heat until the slices turn pale gold. Never brown them fast.
Add the pepper flakes off the heat and let them bloom in the warm oil.
Toss the drained pasta with the oil, a splash of pasta water, and the parsley until glossy.
Serve immediately; there is no second act for this one.

title: Coconut Chicken Curry
description: A mild, creamy weeknight curry that mostly looks after itself. Serve over rice with a squeeze of lime.
steps: Brown the chicken in the oil over high heat, then set aside.
Soften the onion, then add the garlic, ginger, and curry powder and cook for a minute.
Return the chicken, add the coconut milk and tomatoes, and simmer uncovered for 20 minutes.
Meanwhile cook the rice.
Season the curry with salt and finish with lime juice to taste.

title: Red Lentil Dahl
description: Cheap, fast, and better on day two. Red lentils collapse into a soft, spoonable stew without any help.
steps: Rinse the lentils until the water runs clear.
Fry the onion in the oil until golden, then add the garlic, ginger, and spices for a minute.
Add the lentils, tomatoes, and 1 litre of water. Simmer until the lentils have collapsed, 20-25 minutes.
Swirl in the butter and season generously with salt.
Serve with rice or bread and a dollop of yogurt.

title: Beef Chili
description: A slow-flavored, fast-cooking chili: one pot, done in under an hour, and the leftovers are the point.
steps: Brown the beef in the oil in a heavy pot, breaking it up; pour off excess fat.
Add the onion and pepper and cook until soft, about 5 minutes.
Stir in the garlic and spices for a minute, then the tomatoes.
Simmer uncovered for 30 minutes, stirring now and then.
Add the beans and cook 5 more minutes. Season and serve. It is better the next day.

title: Mujadara
description: Lentils and rice under a mountain of crispy fried onions. Humble, vegan, and quietly one of the best dishes in the library.
steps: Simmer the lentils in plenty of water until just tender, 15-20 minutes, then drain.
Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat, stirring rarely, until deeply browned and crisp, at least 20 minutes. Set half aside.
Add the rice, cumin, and salt to the pan with the remaining onions and stir to coat.
Add the lentils and 500 ml of water; cover and cook on low for 15 minutes.
Rest 5 minutes off the heat, then top with the reserved crispy onions.

title: Minestrone
description: A vegetable soup that eats like a meal. Flexible about the vegetables; stubborn about the parmesan rind.
steps: Sweat the onion, carrots, and celery in the oil until soft, 10 minutes.
Add the garlic, then the tomatoes and 1.5 litres of water. Drop in the parmesan rind.
Simmer 15 minutes, then add the beans, pasta, and cabbage.
Cook until the pasta is done, 8-10 minutes. Fish out the rind.
Serve with grated parmesan and olive oil on top.

title: Sheet-Pan Chicken and Potatoes
description: Lemon, garlic, and a hot oven do all the work. Everything cooks on one tray, and the potatoes soak up the chicken juices.
steps: Heat the oven to 220°C.
Toss the chicken, potatoes, lemon, and garlic with the oil, paprika, and salt on a large tray.
Roast for 45-50 minutes, turning the potatoes once, until the chicken skin is crisp.
Rest 5 minutes before serving straight from the tray.

title: Greek Salad
description: No lettuce, no apology. Big tomato wedges, cucumber, olives, and a slab of feta under a bright oregano dressing.
steps: Combine the tomatoes, cucumber, and onion in a broad bowl.
Lay the feta on top in one piece and scatter over the olives.
Dress with the oil, a splash of vinegar, the oregano, and plenty of pepper.
Let it sit 10 minutes before serving so the tomato juices join the dressing.

title: Banana Bread
description: The use-up-the-black-bananas classic. Browning the butter takes it from good to the thing people ask about.
steps: Heat the oven to 175°C and line a loaf tin.
Brown the butter in a pan until it smells nutty, then cool slightly.
Mash the bananas and whisk in the butter, sugar, and eggs.
Fold in the flour, baking powder, salt, and cinnamon until just mixed.
Bake 50-60 minutes until a skewer comes out clean. Cool before slicing, if you can.

title: Miso Salmon Rice Bowl
description: Weeknight-speed dinner that doesn't taste like a compromise: glazed salmon over rice with quick-pickled cucumber.
steps: Cook the rice. Meanwhile, toss the cucumber with the vinegar and a pinch of salt.
Whisk the soy sauce and honey.
Sear the salmon skin-side down in a hot pan for 4 minutes, flip, and brush with the glaze.
Cook 2-3 minutes more until just done, basting again.
Serve over rice with the cucumber, scallion, and sesame seeds.
